title: NHTSA Cruise Crash-Reporting Consent Order
summary: NHTSA records a consent order addressing incomplete automated-driving crash reports submitted by Cruise.
key_findings: The action concerns incomplete reporting under the Standing General Order.
It includes the October 2023 pedestrian crash record.
The case demonstrates that reporting quality itself requires enforcement.
why_it_matters: It supplies a concrete control on the reliability of the operating-safety evidence rail.
ftfn_relevance: Advances one named Phase 55Y reader journey.
Separates the current evidence stage from downstream operation or outcome claims.
Creates a specific next-record watch point.
evidence_limits: One enforcement case cannot characterize all operators.
The order does not by itself provide exposure-adjusted comparative safety evidence.
